label: wire
description: a cylindrical or near-cylindrical rod attached at its base to a parent body and free at its tip. filigree strands and jump-ring wire are wires. the failure mode is the tip diameter falling below the printability or casting floor; the base attachment is a separate clearance concern. the benchmark family that exercises this op is feature-ladder (wire sub-family: cylinders of descending diameter standing on a base plate).
notes: wall measurement on a cylinder is diameter / 2 via ray-cast from the surface normal inward. the harness currently treats wire diameter as minimum_wall_thickness because the mesh inspector measures the thinnest cross-section regardless of declared geometry. when declared ops are wired into the harness the measurement can switch to the declared tip_diameter_mm.

label: stub
description: a short prong-like protrusion — wider than a wire, shorter than a prong, used as a stone seat, decorative boss, or connection nub. the distinction from wire is proportional: a stub's height is comparable to its diameter (aspect ratio near 1) whereas a wire is tall relative to its diameter. the benchmark family that exercises this op is feature-ladder (stub sub-family: short cylinders of descending diameter standing on a base plate).
notes: prong setting stubs are the safety-critical instance: seat depth must not exceed 25% of prong diameter (stuller src-0011). that constraint is not yet in profile-001 and is not exercised by the current benchmark.

label: through hole
description: a void that penetrates the full thickness of a body, typically cylindrical. includes pilot divots (blind holes used as drill guides after casting) and evacuation holes in hollow shells. the failure modes are: diameter too small for investment to flow cleanly, depth-to-diameter ratio too high for consistent fill, and placement intersecting a thin wall. the benchmark family that exercises this op is feature-ladder (hole sub-family: through-holes of descending diameter in a base plate).
notes: morris and watson (src-0022) and stuller (src-0011) both express depth <= diameter as the governing ratio. formlabs (src-0015) extends it to all negative features. cooksongold (src-0010) says avoid holes under 0.5 mm entirely and fill them in cad.

label: emboss
description: raised relief standing above the parent surface, created by adding material outward. includes raised lettering, milgrain, raised logos, and decorative bosses that are part of the parent body surface rather than freestanding elements. the neck between the relief feature and the surface is the critical dimension: too thin and the relief shears off during finishing. the benchmark family that exercises this op is feature-ladder (text sub-family: linear_extrude + text() raising glyphs above the base plate).
notes: the cooksongold / stuller consensus on raised text is: neck (stroke thickness) >= 0.30 mm, height <= 0.60 mm, spacing >= 0.30 mm. morris and watson (src-0022) lowers the height ceiling to 0.50 mm. contradiction-011 (unresolved) blocks promotion of ctr-engrave-001. the feature-ladder benchmark exercises this op at the three conflicting rule-set values.

label: engrave
description: recessed relief cut into the parent surface via material removal (difference operation). includes recessed lettering, channel engraving, decorative incisions, and name engravings. the failure modes are: remaining wall below floor after cut, depth-to-width ratio too high for investment or wax to fill the void cleanly, and draft angle insufficient to release the investment. the benchmark family that exercises this op is engrave-recess (text cut into a base plate via difference, at sourced depth values).
notes: cooksongold (src-0010, evid-feat-003): recessed min width 0.30 mm, max depth 0.50 mm, spacing 0.30 mm. stuller (src-0011, evid-feat-004): recessed min width 0.30 mm, max depth 2x width. materialise (src-0001, evid-engrave-002): max depth-to-width ratio 1:1, min remaining wall 0.35 mm. hoover & strong (src-0007, evid-engrave-001): max depth 0.50 mm, min width 0.75 mm, draft 7 deg. conflict on depth-to-width ratio (1:1 vs 2:1) is unresolved and noted in contradiction register.
